
{{alias}}( x[, options] )
    Returns a new ndarray containing the one-dimensional discrete Fourier
    transform of a real-valued input ndarray.

    The returned ndarray has a complex-valued floating-point data type
    determined by the input data type. For example, `float64` maps to
    `complex128`.

    The returned ndarray has a length of `floor(N/2) + 1`, where `N` is the
    length of the sequence to transform.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x: ndarray
        Input array. Must have a real-valued or "generic" data type.

    options: Object (optional)
        Function options.

    options.n: integer (optional)
        Number of points over which to compute the transform. If not provided,
        the number of points is equal to the length of the input array. If the
        value is greater than the length of the input array, the input is
        zero-padded. If the value is less than the length of the input array,
        the input is truncated.

    options.normalize: string (optional)
        Normalization mode. Must be one of the following: 'backward' (default),
        'ortho', or 'forward'. When set to 'backward', no normalization is
        applied. When set to 'ortho', the result is scaled by `1/sqrt(n)`.
        When set to 'forward', the result is scaled by `1/n`.

    Returns
    -------
    out: ndarray
        Output array.

    Examples
    --------
    > var x = {{alias:@stdlib/ndarray/array}}( [ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 ] );
    > var out = {{alias}}( x )
    <ndarray>


{{alias}}.assign( x, out[, options] )
    Computes the one-dimensional discrete Fourier transform of a real-valued
    input ndarray and assigns the results to a provided output ndarray.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x: ndarray
        Input array. Must have a real-valued or "generic" data type.

    out: ndarray
        Output array. Must have a complex-valued floating-point data type.

    options: Object (optional)
        Function options.

    options.n: integer (optional)
        Number of points over which to compute the transform. If not provided,
        the number of points is equal to the length of the input array. If the
        value is greater than the length of the input array, the input is
        zero-padded. If the value is less than the length of the input array,
        the input is truncated.

    options.normalize: string (optional)
        Normalization mode. Must be one of the following: 'backward' (default),
        'ortho', or 'forward'. When set to 'backward', no normalization is
        applied. When set to 'ortho', the result is scaled by `1/sqrt(n)`.
        When set to 'forward', the result is scaled by `1/n`.

    Returns
    -------
    out: ndarray
        Output array.

    Examples
    --------
    > var x = {{alias:@stdlib/ndarray/array}}( [ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 ] );
    > var opts = { 'dtype': 'complex128' };
    > var out = {{alias:@stdlib/ndarray/zeros}}( [ 3 ], opts );
    > var v = {{alias}}.assign( x, out )
    <ndarray>
    > var bool = ( v === out )
    true

    See Also
    --------
